mitigation_mechanism: In semi-arid Burkina Faso and Niger, zaï pits and stone bunds let more water infiltrate and conserve soil moisture, so rainfed crops suffer less from dry spells at the onset of and during the rainy season [ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1]. Zaï gave 300 – 400 kg of sorghum in a year of low rainfall where untreated land yielded 0 kg/ha, only fields treated with tassa produced a harvest in the 1990 drought year, and crops behind stone bunds could yield two to three times more than control plots during dry years [ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. In semi-arid Brazil, water from runoff ponds applied as supplemental irrigation during in-season dry spells has reduced farming risk in years of irregular rainfall, and production-cistern water can reduce animal mortality in periods of more severe drought [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. In Burkina Faso, zaï of 30–40 cm and 1-m half-moon plots mitigated the impact of dry spells by retaining moisture for 2-3 weeks [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]. A Burkina Faso review concludes that soil and water conservation techniques helped reduce vulnerability to drought and famine [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7].
caveats: The buffer runs out in severe or prolonged drought: Brazilian subsurface dams tended to dry up through a rainless year and, because of their small size, do not withstand long droughts, which records no benefit rather than damage to the works, and Niger farm families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated deficit of 28 percent in years with low rainfall [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3, ev_food_security_kabo04_1]. The large yield contrasts are author estimates or a secondary citation rather than controlled measurements, the Niger deficit figure is itself cited from another study and does not isolate a single practice, and the Brazilian pond and cistern statements are an institutional assertion and a statement of potential without data from an upper-middle-income country [ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s, ev_food_security_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. The Burkina Faso half-moon and zaï moisture finding is the authors' statement about dry spells, for pits filled with compost [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]. That Burkina Faso conclusion is the author's overall judgement, with no measured drought-year contrast behind it [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7].

mitigation_mechanism: Zaï and tassa pits increase infiltration and the water retention capacity of the soil, so crops suffer less from drought spells at the onset of and during the rainy season [ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1]. In rainfall-deficit periods zaï allowed cereals to be grown on degraded crusted soils in Burkina Faso, gave sorghum in a low-rainfall year where untreated land yielded nothing, and only tassa fields produced a harvest in the 1990 drought in Niger [ev_crop_yield_roose93_3, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s]. In Zimbabwe first-year planting-basin farmers obtained 1520 kg of maize per hectare against 368 kg on conventional plots in the 2006/07 season, which the source calls a drought year [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_1]. In a Kenyan trial, tied ridges in long rains with dry spells gave 2.53 against 1.82 t per hectare without inputs (not significant) and 4.10 against 3.15 t per hectare with manure and fertiliser [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_1, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_3]. Chololo pits in Tanzania are reported to mitigate drought effects [ev_crop_yield_ngur26_7]. Studies cited in a conservation agriculture meta-analysis report yields 10–100% higher than conventional tillage in relatively dry years [ev_crop_yield_rusin11_4, ev_crop_yield_rusin11_6]. Against the fertilised conventional arm in the same Zimbabwe budget the contrast was 1520 against 400 kg per hectare [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_2]. In an Ethiopian Rift Valley trial, the plots without mulch were the ones particularly affected by the dry spells of the season [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1]. In on-farm conservation-farming trials in Kenya, Tanzania and Ethiopia the largest yield difference over conventional ploughing came in rainy seasons with low rainfall, when the practice maximises rainfall infiltration so the crop can bridge short periods of dry spell [ev_crop_yield_rock09_15]. In Zambia's 2001/2 season of very scattered rainfall, maize in hand-hoe conservation-farming basins yielded 3,054 kg per hectare against 1,339 kg under ploughing, which the authors say showcased the water-harvesting benefits of the basins [ev_crop_yield_hagg03_1].
caveats: Zaï only reduces the impact of a dry spell of two to three weeks, and only where soil water storage capacity is at least 50 mm [ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1]. In the Kenyan trial's short rains with meteorological droughts, tied ridging gave no advantage (0.52 against 0.53 t per hectare without inputs, 1.17 against 1.27 with manure and fertiliser) because there was little or no rainwater to hold in the basins [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_2, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_4, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_5, ev_soil_water_retention_ndun23_1]. Conservation agriculture can reverse in extremes: in long-term Zimbabwe trials mulched and reduced-tillage maize yielded considerably less than conventional tillage in extreme seasons, and a study cited in the same meta-analysis reports yields 5–20% lower in wet years [ev_crop_yield_rusin11_7, ev_crop_yield_rusin11_4]. The zaï and tassa contrasts are author estimates, the Zimbabwe planting-basin gain also carries manure and fertiliser, and the Kenyan tied-ridging result comes from a single-site trial [ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_mazv09_1, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_1]. The Ethiopian dry-spell finding is a field observation of which plots wilted, not a tested yield contrast [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1]. Water harvesting is not irrigation, and the new primaries mark the limit: at the more arid Kenyan sites of Laikipia and Machakos each site recorded complete crop failures in two out of three and four seasons, with 0 kg per hectare of maize harvested at Machakos due to meteorological drought, and the conservation-farming treatments did not avert it [ev_crop_yield_rock09_10]. The East African low-rainfall gain is for the best system per site, ripping or pitting usually with fertiliser, so it is bundled with reduced tillage and fertiliser, and the authors read it as a trend from their own figure [ev_crop_yield_rock09_15]. The Zambia 2001/2 basin contrast is a raw comparison in a single season with no normal-year reference, and most basin farmers received hybrid seed, fertiliser and lime on credit, so part of the gap is the input package [ev_crop_yield_hagg03_1].

justification.mechanism: Zaï and tassa pits increase infiltration and the water retention capacity of the soil, so crops suffer less from drought spells at the onset of and during the rainy season [ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1]. In rainfall-deficit periods zaï allowed cereals to be grown on degraded crusted soils in Burkina Faso, gave sorghum in a low-rainfall year where untreated land yielded nothing, and only tassa fields produced a harvest in the 1990 drought in Niger [ev_crop_yield_roose93_3, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s]. In Zimbabwe first-year planting-basin farmers obtained 1520 kg of maize per hectare against 368 kg on conventional plots in the 2006/07 season, which the source calls a drought year [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_1]. In a Kenyan trial, tied ridges in long rains with dry spells gave 2.53 against 1.82 t per hectare without inputs (not significant) and 4.10 against 3.15 t per hectare with manure and fertiliser [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_1, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_3]. Chololo pits in Tanzania are reported to mitigate drought effects [ev_crop_yield_ngur26_7]. Studies cited in a conservation agriculture meta-analysis report yields 10–100% higher than conventional tillage in relatively dry years [ev_crop_yield_rusin11_4, ev_crop_yield_rusin11_6]. Against the fertilised conventional arm in the same Zimbabwe budget the contrast was 1520 against 400 kg per hectare [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_2]. In an Ethiopian Rift Valley trial, the plots without mulch were the ones particularly affected by the dry spells of the season [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1]. In on-farm conservation-farming trials in Kenya, Tanzania and Ethiopia the largest yield difference over conventional ploughing came in rainy seasons with low rainfall, when the practice maximises rainfall infiltration so the crop can bridge short periods of dry spell [ev_crop_yield_rock09_15]. In Zambia's 2001/2 season of very scattered rainfall, maize in hand-hoe conservation-farming basins yielded 3,054 kg per hectare against 1,339 kg under ploughing, which the authors say showcased the water-harvesting benefits of the basins [ev_crop_yield_hagg03_1].
justification.conditionality: Zaï only reduces the impact of a dry spell of two to three weeks, and only where soil water storage capacity is at least 50 mm [ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1]. In the Kenyan trial's short rains with meteorological droughts, tied ridging gave no advantage (0.52 against 0.53 t per hectare without inputs, 1.17 against 1.27 with manure and fertiliser) because there was little or no rainwater to hold in the basins [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_2, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_4, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_5, ev_soil_water_retention_ndun23_1]. Conservation agriculture can reverse in extremes: in long-term Zimbabwe trials mulched and reduced-tillage maize yielded considerably less than conventional tillage in extreme seasons, and a study cited in the same meta-analysis reports yields 5–20% lower in wet years [ev_crop_yield_rusin11_7, ev_crop_yield_rusin11_4]. The zaï and tassa contrasts are author estimates, the Zimbabwe planting-basin gain also carries manure and fertiliser, and the Kenyan tied-ridging result comes from a single-site trial [ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_mazv09_1, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_1]. The Ethiopian dry-spell finding is a field observation of which plots wilted, not a tested yield contrast [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1]. Water harvesting is not irrigation, and the new primaries mark the limit: at the more arid Kenyan sites of Laikipia and Machakos each site recorded complete crop failures in two out of three and four seasons, with 0 kg per hectare of maize harvested at Machakos due to meteorological drought, and the conservation-farming treatments did not avert it [ev_crop_yield_rock09_10]. The East African low-rainfall gain is for the best system per site, ripping or pitting usually with fertiliser, so it is bundled with reduced tillage and fertiliser, and the authors read it as a trend from their own figure [ev_crop_yield_rock09_15]. The Zambia 2001/2 basin contrast is a raw comparison in a single season with no normal-year reference, and most basin farmers received hybrid seed, fertiliser and lime on credit, so part of the gap is the input package [ev_crop_yield_hagg03_1].

mitigation_mechanism: Terraces, stone bunds and infiltration trenches slow and spread runoff on slopes: terraces lowered mean runoff and flood peaks on small mountain plots, stone bunds lower peak discharges at the foot of the slope, trenches significantly reduced plot runoff across the reviewed studies, and a combined treatment in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment reduced flood runoff volume, clipped peaks and lengthened flood duration [ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_1, ev_runoff_reduction_locat20_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s]. A check-dam review cites check dams mitigating flooding and significantly reducing peak flow in Iran and check-dam sequences proving effective against strong floods in Italian torrents, and small hill dams in Morocco are credited with damping damage during the serious 2002-2003 floods [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1]. Spate and diversion structures in Yemen are reported to control floods, users of small reservoirs in Ghana perceive flood limitation as a benefit, compacted hill terraces in Uttarakhand, India are credited with limiting flood and landslide damage, and in heavy rain stone bunds protect land in Burkina Faso from rapid flow [ev_flood_hazard_yem12_4, ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7, ev_erosion_hazard_zoug14_2]. WOCAT compilers in Burkina Faso, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, Tunisia and Uzbekistan rate flooding as reduced and say how: rain retained where it falls, a dam or series of dams acting as a downstream buffer, stone lines and walls cutting peak flows, and structures slowing runoff velocity [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1537_2012_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_flood_impacts]. Embrapa credits its barraginhas, small runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths in Brazil, with easing floods as well [ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].
caveats: The sub-practices disagree, and the split runs through terracing: bunds and terraces that slow and spread runoff on the slope lowered peak discharges, while structures that divert runoff did the opposite — diversion banquettes in Niger raised peak discharges and runoff-diversion systems accelerate concentration time, with serious gully risk if the dikes break [ev_flood_hazard_roose94_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_3]. In-situ, runoff-catchment and spate rows each show a moderate reduction on their own, so whether the practice eases or worsens flooding depends on whether it holds water in place or concentrates it. Storage size matters too: larger sand dams increase flooding risk, and a check-dam review finds a minimal effect against extreme floods, especially where structures were ill-designed and not maintained [ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_3]. Catchment-level terrace evidence is scarce, most measured results are at plot or hillslope scale, the Tunisian catchment result bundles rangeland closure and gully stone-filling with the bunds, and the Italian check-dam cases are mountain torrent control in a high-income setting rather than farm water harvesting [ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2]. The barraginha flood statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, unmeasured, and a landscape-scale effect rather than one on the adopting farm [ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].

mitigation_mechanism: Practices that hold water in the field can backfire in wet conditions: stone bunds can waterlog parts of the field in wet years, millet behind stone bunds can suffer waterlogging when monthly rainfall exceeds 200 mm, and in the humid Sudanian zone of Cameroon sorghum in zaï pits yielded less than on flat-cultivated fields [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4]. A conservation agriculture meta-analysis adds that 92% of the data show mulch cover in high-rainfall areas lowering maize yields through waterlogging [ev_crop_yield_rusin11_3]. In an Ethiopian Rift Valley trial, waterlogging lasting 3–5 days during early maize growth also affected the mulching and basin treatments, whose waterlogged plants had yellow leaves and stunted growth [ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_1, ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_2]. In a Kenyan on-farm trial, ridged plots with fertiliser at the relatively wetter sub-humid Rachuonyo site gave the lowest yields, slightly below conventional practice, which the authors say can probably be explained by waterlogging caused by ridging [ev_crop_yield_rock09_6].
caveats: Every unit points the same way, but the harm is tied to wet years, very wet months or high-rainfall zones, and none gives the size of the yield loss or the share of field affected, so this is a warning about placing water-holding practices where water is already in excess rather than a measured penalty [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_rusin11_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4]. The Burkina Faso statements are cited rather than measured, and the Cameroon observation is unpublished work cited by the authors [ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4]. The meta-analysis figure is a share of observations, not an effect size [ev_crop_yield_rusin11_3]. The Ethiopian waterlogging finding is a field observation with no measured yield loss, and the source names a tillage treatment as the one particularly affected, so only part of the harm can be put on mulch and basins [ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_1, ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_2]. The Kenyan ridging loss is the authors' probable explanation rather than a measured waterlogging contrast, and the ridging is bundled with fertiliser; because it comes from using the practice at a wetter site than it suits, it is held out of the production classes as an envelope misfit (a suitability caveat) and counted here as waterlogging evidence [ev_crop_yield_rock09_6].

mitigation_mechanism: Slope failure damages terraces where slopes are unstable or terraces are abandoned: in the Tizi Ouzou region of Algeria 19% of banquettes on marls and clays were damaged by landslides and as many by gullying, and in Mediterranean regions over 50% of abandoned terraces were vulnerable to gully erosion and landslides that collapse the dry-stone walls [ev_climate_shock_arab04_2_av, ev_climate_shock_wei16_1_av]. Among WOCAT compilers, stone check walls and check dams in India are rated as coping only moderately with landslides [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_5210_2019_landslide].
caveats: Other compilers rate stone lines in Tunisia, a masonry check dam in Ethiopia and a continuous bench terrace for tea in Thailand as coping well, and vetiver-hedge bench terraces with trees in Haiti and bench terraces on hilly slopes in Bangladesh as coping very well [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_6610_2022_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_6716_2023_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_4281_2018_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_3223_2017_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_4284_2018_landslide]. The damage figures are secondary citations tied to marl and clay substrates and to abandonment, not to maintained terraces, and the ratings come from a small set of technology sheets rather than measurements [ev_climate_shock_arab04_2_av, ev_climate_shock_wei16_1_av].
